# Chair of Software Engineering – Saarland University

> A leading research group advancing software engineering through studies of program comprehension, product-line engineering, software evolution, and AI-driven optimization.

The Chair of Software Engineering at Saarland University conducts cutting-edge research in software variability, configurable systems, socio-technical analysis, and cognitive science applications to programming. The group is funded by the European Research Council and German Research Foundation, and collaborates with industry partners including Siemens, Bosch, and Airbus.

## Key Topics

- Software Engineering
- Program Comprehension
- Software Evolution
- Product-Line Engineering
- Configurable Systems
- Software Variability
- Socio-Technical Analysis
- AI Optimization
- Program Generation
- Empirical Studies
- Eye-Tracking
- Feature-Oriented Programming
- Cognitive Neuroscience
- Distributed Software Projects
- Performance Analysis

## Core Research

- [Research Overview](https://se.cs.uni-saarland.de/research.php): Research projects in software engineering including automation, variability, and AI optimization
- [Brains on Code](https://se.cs.uni-saarland.de/projects/BrainsOnCode): Cognitive neuroscience project studying how developers comprehend and understand program code
- [Congruence](https://se.cs.uni-saarland.de/projects/congruence): Analyzing socio-technical alignment in large-scale, decentralized, and distributed software projects
- [Pervolution](https://se.cs.uni-saarland.de/projects/pervolution): Studying performance evolution in highly-configurable software systems like Linux
- [Pythia](https://se.cs.uni-saarland.de/projects/pythia): Developing prediction models for sustainable and efficient product-line engineering
- [SafeSPL](https://se.cs.uni-saarland.de/projects/safespl): Correctness verification and safety assurance in feature-oriented software product lines
